title: Hash Length Extension Attack
description: Forge a valid MAC without the secret key by exploiting SHA256(key||message), then fix the server with HMAC. Based on the SEED Hash Length Extension Attack Lab.
outcomes: Understand why SHA256(key||message) is an insecure MAC
Perform a hash length extension attack to forge a MAC
Explain how HMAC prevents the attack

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content:
# Hash Length Extension Attack

* This lab is based on the SEED *Hash Length Extension Attack Lab* by Wenliang Du (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).
* The solution of each level is **required** in later levels. Do not skip ahead.
* Every sandbox has **different flags and keys** - copying another student's flag will not work.
* This game is for educational purposes only. The story is fictitious.

# Scenario

A web server at `www.seedlab-hashlen.com` executes file commands only if the request carries a valid **MAC**. The developer computed the MAC the naive way: `SHA256(key : message)`. You have an account on it, and you have intercepted a request from the **SysAdmin**. Your goal is to abuse the length extension weakness to read a file you are not allowed to read - and then help the developer fix it with HMAC.

You work from the **SEED** workstation (`attacker`). All lab files are in `~/hashlen/`.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
Access the sandbox where you will complete all tasks. When connected, submit **`start`**.

### Sandbox access
1. In the topology overview on the right, right-click on **`attacker`** and click **`Open GUI`**.
2. Log in with username **`user`** and password **`Password123`**.

Alternatively, connect over SSH (easier copy-paste). See the [documentation](https://docs.platform.cyberrange.cz/user-guide-advanced/sandboxes/sandbox-access/#user-access).

Open a terminal and read `~/hashlen/README.txt` before starting.
levels.local_content: This sandbox has not been tested for use with local sandbox.

levels.title: Task 1 - Send a valid request
levels.content:
Warm up by sending a **legitimate** request that the server will accept.

Your uid and MAC key are in `~/hashlen/mykey.txt` (format `uid:key`). Always include `myname=<YourName>` (no spaces) in every request - the server rejects requests without it.

The MAC is `SHA256(key:R)`, where `R` is the argument part of the URL. For example:
```
Key:R = <key>:myname=<YourName>&uid=<uid>&lstcmd=1
MAC   = echo -n "<key>:myname=<YourName>&uid=<uid>&lstcmd=1" | sha256sum
```
Build the request below, including a `download` of **task1.txt**, and send it with a browser or `curl`:
```
http://www.seedlab-hashlen.com/?myname=<YourName>&uid=<uid>&lstcmd=1&download=task1.txt&mac=<mac>
```

**The flag is the value printed in the file content returned by the server.**

hints.title: Where is my key?
hints.content: `cat ~/hashlen/mykey.txt`. The part before the colon is your uid, the part after is the MAC key.

hints.title: How do I compute the MAC?
hints.content: `echo -n "<key>:<arguments>" | sha256sum`. The `-n` matters (no trailing newline). The arguments must match the URL exactly, in the same order.

levels.title: Task 2 - Build the padding
levels.content:
To extend the message you must know the SHA-256 **padding** of the original signed message.

SHA-256 works on 64-byte blocks. Padding is one `0x80` byte, then `0x00` bytes, then an 8-byte big-endian length field equal to the message length **in bits**. Compute the padding for:
```
<key>:myname=<YourName>&uid=<uid>&lstcmd=1
```
(use your own key, name and uid). In a URL, each byte `\xHH` is written `%HH`.

Submit your padding to the checker, which returns the flag if it is correct:
```
http://www.seedlab-hashlen.com/padcheck?myname=<YourName>&uid=<uid>&padding=<url-encoded-padding>
```

**The flag is the value returned by `/padcheck`.**
levels.solution:
Let `n` = byte length of `<key>:myname=<YourName>&uid=<uid>&lstcmd=1`.
Padding = `\x80` + `\x00` * ((55 - n) mod 64) + 8-byte big-endian (n*8).
```
python3 -c 'import struct;n=<n>;print((b"\x80"+b"\x00"*((55-n)%64)+struct.pack(">Q",n*8)).hex())'
```
Then turn the hex into `%HH%HH...` and send it to `/padcheck`.

hints.title: What exactly gets padded?
hints.content: The whole string `key:message`, i.e. `<key>:myname=<YourName>&uid=<uid>&lstcmd=1`. Count its length in bytes - that is `n`.

hints.title: Padding formula
hints.content: One `%80`, then zeros so the total becomes a multiple of 64 leaving room for 8 length bytes: `(55 - n) mod 64` zero bytes, then the 64-bit big-endian value `n*8`.

levels.title: Task 3 - Launch the length extension attack
levels.content:
Now the real attack. You have a request the **SysAdmin** sent, intercepted in `~/hashlen/captured_request.txt`:
```
http://www.seedlab-hashlen.com/?myname=SysAdmin&uid=<admin-uid>&lstcmd=1&mac=<mac>
```
You do **not** know the SysAdmin's key, but the file tells you its length. Using only the captured MAC and the key length, forge a new request that appends `&download=secret.txt` and still has a valid MAC - **without** the key.

Use `~/hashlen/length_ext.c` as a template: set the 8 `c.h[i]` words to the 8 32-bit words of the captured MAC, set the appended string to your extra message, and compile with `gcc length_ext.c -o length_ext -lcrypto`. Insert the padding (Task 2 method, with `n = keylen + len(message)`) between `lstcmd=1` and `&download=secret.txt` in the URL.

**The flag is the value inside secret.txt returned by the server.**
levels.solution:
1. Split the captured 64-hex MAC into 8 words and load them into `c.h[0..7]`.
2. Set `SHA256_Update(&c, "&download=secret.txt", 20)`.
3. `n = keylen + len("myname=SysAdmin&uid=<admin-uid>&lstcmd=1")`; build padding for that `n`.
4. URL: `/?myname=SysAdmin&uid=<admin-uid>&lstcmd=1<%-encoded padding>&download=secret.txt&mac=<program output>`.

hints.title: What goes into c.h[0..7]?
hints.content: The captured MAC is 64 hex chars = 8 groups of 8 hex chars. Each group is one `c.h[i]`, e.g. `c.h[0]=htole32(0x<first 8 hex>)`.

hints.title: What length for the padding?
hints.content: The server already hashed `key:message`. So the padded length is `n = keylen + len(":") ... ` - precisely `len(key) + 1 + len("myname=SysAdmin&uid=<admin-uid>&lstcmd=1")`. The key length is given in the captured file.

hints.title: Where does the padding go in the URL?
hints.content: Right after `lstcmd=1` and before `&download=secret.txt`, URL-encoded as `%HH`. The appended string in the C program must be exactly `&download=secret.txt`.

levels.title: Task 4 - Fix it with HMAC
levels.content:
The developer shipped a fixed server at `/v2/` that verifies the MAC with **HMAC-SHA256** instead of `SHA256(key:message)`. Confirm your Task 3 forge no longer works against `/v2/`, then send a correct HMAC request that downloads **task4.txt**.

Compute `HMAC-SHA256(key, message)` over the argument string:
```python
import hmac, hashlib
mac = hmac.new(key.encode(), message.encode('utf-8','surrogateescape'), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
```
Send:
```
http://www.seedlab-hashlen.com/v2/?myname=<YourName>&uid=<uid>&lstcmd=1&download=task4.txt&mac=<hmac>
```
In your report, explain in one or two sentences **why** the length extension attack fails against HMAC.

**The flag is the value inside task4.txt returned by `/v2/`.**
levels.solution:
```
M='myname=<YourName>&uid=<uid>&lstcmd=1&download=task4.txt'
MAC=$(python3 -c "import hmac,hashlib;print(hmac.new(b'<key>',b'$M',hashlib.sha256).hexdigest())")
curl "http://www.seedlab-hashlen.com/v2/?$M&mac=$MAC"
```
HMAC hashes `key` into the inner and outer blocks (`H((k^opad)||H((k^ipad)||m))`); the attacker cannot extend the inner state without the key, so a forged tag fails.

hints.title: Which endpoint?
hints.content: Use `/v2/` (note the trailing path). The same key from `mykey.txt` still applies.

hints.title: HMAC in one line
hints.content: `python3 -c "import hmac,hashlib;print(hmac.new(b'<key>', b'<message>', hashlib.sha256).hexdigest())"` where `<message>` is the argument string after the `?`.
